description: The study of traditional Paintings, Martial Arts, and Theatre forms under Static GK covers India's rich cultural heritage. This section is highly crucial for direct factual questions asked in competitive exams.

sections.title: Major Paintings of India
sections.description: Traditional folk and tribal paintings belonging to various states of India.

key_associations.extra_info: Also known as Mithila Art, it is characterized by eye-catching geometrical patterns and the use of natural colors.
Created by the Warli tribe, it mainly depicts nature and elements of daily village life using basic geometric shapes.
A traditional cloth-based scroll painting dedicated primarily to Lord Jagannath.
A type of hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile using natural dyes.
A religious scroll painting portraying local folk deities like Pabuji and Devnarayan.
A dot-based tribal art form practiced by the Gond community.
Famous for its rich and flat colors, simple iconic composition, and extensive use of gold foil and precious stones.

important_facts.fact: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters in Madhya Pradesh contain the oldest known rock art in India.
Raja Ravi Varma was an eminent Indian painter famous for beautifully fusing European academic techniques with Indian sensibilities and mythology.

sections.title: Traditional Martial Arts of India
sections.description: Ancient and traditional fighting arts originating from various Indian states.

key_associations.extra_info: Widely considered the oldest surviving martial art form in the world.
A weapon-based martial art associated with the Sikhs, employing primarily wooden sticks and swords.
Part of the Huyen Lallong system; 'Thang' means sword and 'Ta' means spear.
A traditional sport in which a gymnast performs aerial yoga or gymnastic postures on a vertical wooden pole.
An ancient weapon-based martial art that primarily uses a long bamboo staff.
A traditional form of folk wrestling.
Created by Rajputs, its martial movements form the basic steps of the famous Chhau dance.

sections.title: Traditional Theatre Forms of India
sections.description: Prominent regional folk drama and theatre forms practiced across the country.

key_associations.extra_info: A popular folk theatre based on folklore, mythological tales, and stories of romance and bravery.
A highly energetic folk theatre often accompanied by the vibrant Lavani dance.
A traditional folk theatre deeply centered around human emotions.
A musical theatre form historically performed on open-air stages during regional festivals.
A unique blend of dance, music, dialogue, and heavy costumes based primarily on the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
Literally translating to 'street play', it is widely performed during village temple festivals.
A musical folk theatre prominent in the Malwa region.
A traditional religious theatre form initiated by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardeva.

sections.title: Puppetry Forms in India
sections.description: Major puppetry styles utilizing strings, shadows, or gloves.

key_associations.extra_info: The most famous traditional string puppet form of India, made of wood and cloth.
A famous leather shadow puppetry form known for its large and colorful figures.
A shadow puppet form where the puppet size varies according to the depicted character's social status.
A traditional glove puppet form that heavily reflects the style and influence of Kathakali dance.

sections.title: Important Cultural Institutions
sections.description: Key facts regarding national institutions dedicated to the preservation and promotion of Indian arts.

important_facts.fact: Lalit Kala Akademi, the National Academy of Art, was established in New Delhi in 1954 to promote and propagate visual arts.
The National School of Drama (NSD) was set up by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1959 and became an independent entity in 1975.
The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) was established in 1987 in New Delhi as a premier resource center for the study of all major arts.
